title: mixengine-artifact.json
description: Written into the root of every archive this repository publishes. It is the reason the daemon can install a borrowed artifact without knowing anything about how its publisher lays out a directory: the archive keeps that layout, and this file says where things are. An archive without one is not an artifact.

source.description: Whether the payload came from a publisher who already produces something relocatable, or was compiled here. It is recorded because the two age differently: a borrowed artifact goes stale when its publisher moves, a built one when its recipe stops compiling.

upstream.description: Where a borrowed payload came from, kept so a reader can check that what is in the archive is what upstream published — even after upstream has deleted it.

verified_against.description: What the hash was checked against — for PHP on Windows, windows.php.net's own releases.json rather than a hash we computed and then trusted.

project.description: Who published the payload, where that is not simply the runtime's own project: "astral-sh/python-build-standalone", "oneclick/rubyinstaller2".

release.description: The publisher's own identifier for the release this came out of, when it is not the runtime version. python-build-standalone tags by date and RubyInstaller tags by version *and packaging revision*, so two archives of one CPython or one Ruby are told apart here rather than in the index, which is keyed on the runtime version alone.

variant.description: Which asset of that release was taken, where the publisher offers several of the same target — python-build-standalone's `install_only_stripped` against its `install_only`.

added.description: Paths this repository wrote into an otherwise borrowed archive, so that a reader comparing it against upstream finds the difference stated rather than deducing it. There is one at the time of writing: Windows CPython archives get a `Scripts/pip.cmd`, because upstream ships the pip package with no entry point and a generated `pip.exe` would carry an absolute interpreter path into a tree that is going to move.

removed.description: Paths taken *out* of an otherwise borrowed archive, for the same reason `added` states the ones put in. Removal is reserved for a file that would make the archive work on some machines and not others: Linux CPython before 3.13 ships a `_crypt` module linked against a libxcrypt no archive here carries, which is present on Debian and Ubuntu and absent on a default Fedora. Deleting it is what lets `smoke.relocated` keep meaning that nothing in the tree reaches outside it.

recipe.description: For a built payload: the tool and version that produced it, e.g. "static-php-cli 2.7.1".

smoke.description: What was actually proven about this archive before it was published, on the machine that built it. `php -v` alone is not enough: it passes with a broken extension_dir, because the built-in extensions are static and never consult it.

relocated.description: The archive was extracted, moved to an unrelated directory, and exercised from there — never from where it was produced.

openssl.description: The TLS library the archive was proven to *call*, as it names itself. Recorded because it is the one thing about a bundled runtime a user cannot see from outside, and because every runtime here carries its own: a Python, a Ruby and a Node.js installed on one machine are three different OpenSSLs.

loaded_extension.description: A shared extension that was loaded from extension_dir after relocation. Absent when the build has none to load.

loaded_extensions.description: Every shared extension that was loaded after relocation, where the recipe proves all of them rather than one. Proving one shows extension_dir is honoured; proving all shows no extension built into an archive that cannot load it — which is a separate failure, invisible in a build log, and the usual shape of it is an extension whose symbols come from another extension that has to be loaded first.
